summary: Flint Island light off Cape Breton's east coast: first lit November 1856, a concrete tower of 1961 to 1963 still operating, Coast Guard property reached by boat only.

lens.note: Third-order dioptric quadruple flashing light installed in 1910 (report for the twelve months to 31 March 1910); lamp burned petroleum vapour under a mantle (LF).

structures.note: Province of Nova Scotia tower with a detached dwelling; burned on the night of 31 August 1864 (LF).
Second tower, similar to the first (LF); NSLPS gives 1866 with a question mark.
Reinforced concrete tower of 62 ft (18.9 m), built 1909 to 1910; the report's tender list gives 62 feet; LF says hexagonal; replaced 1961 to 1963.
Present tower; LF gives work from 1961 and the register gives 1963. Register calls it octagonal; the Coast Guard list says hexagonal. White with red top.
Three new dwellings built at the same time as the present tower (LF).

staffing.note: LF says the last keepers left when the light was automated in 1985; NSLPS gives automated by 1987; the register says de-staffed in the late 1980s.

access.note: Canadian Coast Guard property, reached by boat only; the tower is closed to visitors (LF; NSLPS).

events.note: Lit 1 November 1856 by keeper George Cann, the only light the Province built that year (LF). NSLPS gives Date Lit Nov 01 1856.
Tower burned on the night of 31 August 1864 (LF). NSLPS gives 1 August 1865 (conflict).
Second tower built, very similar to the first, same flash every fifteen seconds (LF). NSLPS gives 1866 (?).
Men carrying supplies to the island were carried out to sea and spent nine days exposed before reaching shore; the Department gave $600 to be divided among them (LF).
Oscar ashore on Flint Island, floated off. Listed under the company's fiscal year 1907-8; the entry itself gives June 11 with no year.

Three-inch duplicate diaphone plant in a wooden fog alarm building, bought from the Canadian Fog Signal Company for $8,100 (report for the twelve months to 31 March 1909). LF dates the building to 1908.
New concrete lighthouse built 1909 to 1910 (report to 31 March 1910; register gives 1910 and calls it the third lighthouse).
Third-order dioptric quadruple flashing light installed, 74 ft above high water (report to 31 March 1910).
27 April 1911: tug Douglas E. Thomas sent to search for a disabled sailboat with two men, reported off Flint Island, as a storm approached. Outcome not recorded in the list.
Raymond Martell drowned off the northeast part of the island on 23 March 1933 (LF). Another boat accident on 15 October 1933 (LF).
Harold Martell died in January 1940 after a burst appendix; his father took him by boat to the hospital at Glace Bay (LF).
29 August 1961: temporary lantern put on the dwelling while the old tower was torn down and the new one begun (LF).
Present concrete tower: register gives 1963 as its date and says it replaced the 1910 tower; 17.8 m (CCG).
Two diesel generators; oil vapour changed to a 1,000 watt bulb; electric motor to turn the lens (LF).
Electric foghorn replaced the diaphone; staff reduced to two keepers (LF).
Automated; the remaining keepers left (LF). NSLPS: by 1987. Register: late 1980s.
NSLPS list gives an electric lantern with group flashing white (25 s) and a seasonal fog signal; the current Coast Guard entry is LFl W 6s. Disputed.

corrections.why: The Canadian Coast Guard List of Lights (entry 770) gives 46 10 51.0 N, 059 46 13.2 W for Flint Island, about 60 m from the OpenStreetMap position in the record. Reviewed by a human, not applied.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Lighthouse Friends dates the fire to the night of 31 August 1864 and the second tower to 1865. NSLPS dates the fire to 1 August 1865 and gives the replacement as 1866 with a question mark. Both are shown in the story; the Department's reports from 1867 to 1899 are not in the corpus, so neither was checked against an official record.

The Department's reports for the twelve months to 31 March 1909 and 1910 date the fog alarm and the new concrete tower to 1909 to 1910, which agrees with Lighthouse Friends (building 1909) and NSLPS (third tower 1909). The register calls the 1910 tower the third lighthouse.

Lighthouse Friends gives work beginning 29 August 1961; NSLPS gives 1961 to 1962; the register and the Coast Guard record give 1963 for the present tower. The story gives the range and names the source for each date.

The register calls the present tower octagonal; the Coast Guard list and Lighthouse Friends call the 1910 and present towers hexagonal. The record does not settle it, and the story does not state the shape of the present tower.
Lighthouse Friends says 1985, NSLPS says by 1987, the register says the late 1980s. The story gives all three.
NSLPS's 1992 entry gives a group flashing white (25 s); the Coast Guard list gives LFl W 6s, which the record carries. The record's value is used.

notes_for_editor: The narrative rests on Lighthouse Friends for the keepers, the 1864 fire, the 1869 and 1933 to 1940 accounts (paraphrased; facts only, Lighthouse Friends is all rights reserved) and the 1961 start of the present tower. The official reports (Marine Branch, 1901 to 1911) check the 1909 to 1910 tower and fog alarm, the 1911 search and the keepers Helm and McKenzie. Both keeper rows were matched by position in OCR'd tables (scan pp. 261 and 232) and were checked on the page images on 2026-10-27: Helm on printed p. 150 (appointed July 31, 1883) and McKenzie on printed p. 219 (appointed November 19, 1903), both against Flint Island. The 1910 tender row (Flint island items 1 to 5, including the 62-foot hexagonal concrete tower, item 4) was also checked on its page image (printed p. 79). The 1908 'Oscar' line is in a list headed fiscal year 1907-8 with no year in the entry; the story says so. The Dominion Coal Company lists are vessels-assisted lists, not casualty reports. The October 1933 boat account in Lighthouse Friends is inconsistent about who was lost; a Cape Breton newspaper for October 1933 would settle it. Chronicling America searches (Flint Island with lighthouse, 1856 to 1915) returned nothing relevant. Robert Spears is named only in the register's public role. No photographs were mirrored: the Lighthouse Friends and NSLPS photographs are not licensed for reuse here. Access: Lighthouse Friends writes 'Grounds open, tower closed'. The story does not repeat 'grounds open': the island is Coast Guard property reached only by boat, and no source read gives public landing rights. Editor to confirm before the access label goes live.
